title: Mobility-state- and handover-direction-aware analytical and machine learning-based HCP optimization in 5G heterogeneous networks
content:
by Fozia Panhwer, Muhammad Mujtaba Shaikh, Beenish Ansari, Iqra Ameer, Mohamed A. Elmagzoub, Asadullah Shaikh

The use of ultra-dense small cells in 5G heterogeneous networks increases capacity, coverage and spectral efficiency, but it also complicates mobility management. In dense macro-small-cell networks, user devices often cross cells with varying coverage, transmit power, and propagation conditions, which can lead to high risks of radio-link failure, handover failure, ping-pong handover and unnecessary handover. These problems are exacerbated by using fixed handover-control settings, in which a single-value handover margin and time-to-trigger cannot provide a good trade-off across UE velocities and handover directions. In this paper, we propose a mobility-state- and handover-direction-aware HCP optimization for 5G HetNets while retaining the Event A3 handover scheme, state-based handover flow and radio-link-monitoring framework. The proposed framework is simulated with 3D geometry with user height, 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa/UMi propagation models, and a repeatable two-tier macro-small-cell deployment. Four controllers are compared with the same settings: fixed A3, an analytical adaptive controller, tabular Q-learning, and an improved deep Q-network (DQN). The analytical adaptive controller optimizes HOM and TTT based on the UE velocity and handover direction (macro to small, small to macro, and same-tier handovers), and the learning-based controllers use a multi-KPI reward to learn discrete HOM-TTT actions. Across the tested UE velocities, tabular Q-learning improves the principal mobility-robustness KPIs relative to fixed A3, while DQN provides the best observed mean multi-KPI balance among the four controllers. The DQN trend is also consistent with recent ML/DRL handover-optimization studies while retaining the conventional Event A3, finite-state handover, and radio-link-monitoring framework. Because the policy-level comparison is based on three evaluation runs, the reported uncertainty measures are interpreted descriptively and the conclusions are limited to the tested simulation conditions.
author: Fozia Panhwer
